note: On a computer, the player now sits right above the words of the song that is playing. A button on the player bar lets it float in a corner instead.
Hail, Gladdening Light, a reader request, from the September 13 evening service. It is not in the Trinity Hymnal, so it has no hymn number.
Be Thou My Vision has a recording from the November 15 evening service. It stops by itself when the song ends.
Hark can count visits and listening time without a name or an address. It stays quiet when the browser asks not to be tracked.
Songs taken from a Faith Presbyterian bulletin now link to that bulletin.
Moving the pointer over the small player does not drag it. A click opens the song, and it follows only while the button is down.
Leave a song and a small player floats above the bar. Tap it to open that song, with the words under the video.
A song keeps playing while you move around Hark, and the player bar stays up. Where the device allows it, the song title can show with play, pause, and next.
Play all and Auto play all are on the song list, on a search, and on each song. Auto play all follows hymn number from wherever a song was started.
Play next song moves through the list. Auto play all keeps going through the book by number.
Play all is on the home page and the themes list. A new copy of Hark loads as soon as it is published.
Play all the songs in a season. Each recording stops when the song ends.
